record.paper_title: THE LYAPIN’S NOTEBOOK: A COLLECTION OF UNSOLVED PROBLEMS IN SEMIGROUP THEORY
record.context_brief: Separating free semigroups by identical inclusions
record.original_question: Describe ordinary semigroup varieties whose finitely generated free semigroups can be separated from one another by identical inclusions.

evidence.quote:
Problem 6.6. (G. Mashevitzky) Describe ordinary semigroup varieties such that their finitely
generated free semigroups can be separated from each other by identical inclusions.
          The variety of semilattices satisfies this condition ([7, 8]).

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Background and definitions. Let $X = \{x_1, x_2, \ldots\}$ be a countably infinite alphabet and let $X^+$ denote the free semigroup on $X$. An identity is a formal expression $u = v$ with $u, v \in X^+$; an identical inclusion (in the sense of Lyapin) is a formal expression of the form
$$u \in \{w_1, w_2, \ldots, w_k\},$$
where $u, w_1, \ldots, w_k \in X^+$. A semigroup $S$ satisfies the identical inclusion $u \in \{w_1, \ldots, w_k\}$ if for every homomorphism $\varphi : X^+ \to S$ one has $\varphi(u) \in \{\varphi(w_1), \ldots, \varphi(w_k)\}$.

A (semigroup) variety $\mathcal{V}$ is, as usual, a class of semigroups defined by some set of identities; for each $n \geq 1$, the $n$-generated free semigroup of $\mathcal{V}$ is denoted $F_n(\mathcal{V})$. Say that the finitely generated free semigroups of $\mathcal{V}$ are separated from each other by identical inclusions if for every pair of positive integers $m \neq n$ there exists an identical inclusion that is satisfied in exactly one of $F_m(\mathcal{V})$ and $F_n(\mathcal{V})$.

Problem. Describe all (ordinary) semigroup varieties $\mathcal{V}$ with the property that the finitely generated free semigroups $F_1(\mathcal{V}), F_2(\mathcal{V}), F_3(\mathcal{V}), \ldots$ are pairwise separated from each other by identical inclusions. (As a known instance, the variety of semilattices has this property.)
artifact.status_search_result: The problem appears in a recent compilation of unsolved problems in semigroup theory (Lyapin's notebook). Related work by Mashevitzky and collaborators on inclusive varieties (including a 2025 Algebra Universalis paper on nonelementary inclusive varieties) addresses surrounding questions but no source found provides a description answering the problem in the stated generality. Only the semilattice case is known.

status_evidence.title: Nonelementary inclusive varieties of groups and semigroups
status_evidence.snippet: Discusses identical inclusions of Lyapin and inclusive varieties; cites Mashevitzky's results on semilattices and lists open directions.
status_evidence.claim: Recent work investigates inclusive varieties but does not provide a general description of varieties whose finitely generated free semigroups are separated by identical inclusions.
